comments.author: @7th-house
comments.text: As a dentist that has practiced for over 20 years, I have to correct the part about how long it takes a human dentist to prep (or drill) on a tooth for a crown. It only takes 5-15 min for a dentist to do the drilling. Modern dental offices can sometimes fabricate the ceramic crown in the office while the patient waits, and complete the entire treatment in one visit. The longest part of the procedure is fabricating the crown, whether it is done in the office or sent to a dental lab.

comments.author: @spectator59
comments.text: As humans who live with dogs know, barks can be used as a form of communication, but they aren't language. Hunger, pain, affection, curiosity -- sure, but dogs don't use concepts the way humans do. They can understand certain words, at least in a broad sense or by tone, but that's a mostly unidirectional path. We need something more like those big panels of buttons, each of which generates a word when pressed by the dog (or cat), but that doesn't require years of training. Including smells and auditory inputs would also be crucial.
